questions.q: How does CSDM organize CMDB data, according to this lesson?
options: Alphabetically by CI name
Into a small number of distinct layers, each with a different role
Into a single flat table with no grouping
Randomly, since layer assignment doesn't matter
questions.explain: CSDM groups data by role — foundational, planning, and operational — rather than storing everything undifferentiated.

questions.q: What belongs in the foundational/shared layer?
options: Only services that have already failed an outage
Proposed applications that haven't been approved yet
Locations, companies, business units, and core infrastructure CIs that other layers depend on
Nothing — this layer is intentionally left empty
questions.explain: Foundational data is the base everything else builds on; a service can't be modeled meaningfully without it.

questions.q: What kind of data lives in the design-time/planning layer?
options: Services and applications being planned or built, but not yet live in production
Only data about CIs that have been permanently retired
Live production services actively supported today
Historical Incident records from closed tickets
questions.explain: The planning layer tracks intent and future state — proposed or in-development work, not what's currently running.

questions.q: What goes wrong if planning-stage and operational data are not kept separate?
options: Nothing — mixing them has no practical effect
CIs would be deleted automatically
Impact analysis and portfolio planning both get confused, since neither can tell what's genuinely live from what's still proposed
ServiceNow would stop allowing any new CIs to be created
questions.explain: Impact analysis should only trace what's genuinely live, and portfolio planning needs visibility into the pipeline without live-production noise — mixing the two undermines both.

questions.q: What is the live/operational layer meant to represent?
options: Services and CIs actively running and supported in production right now
Services that exist only on a future roadmap
Applications still being coded and tested
A historical archive of decommissioned infrastructure
questions.explain: The operational layer is what's actually live today — outages here affect real users right now.
